text:
alex: Quick pre-oncall sync — I'm taking over tonight (UTC+1). Quick checklist: VPN access, pager, SSH for oncall jumpbox, runbooks verified. Ping if anything broken.

maria: Updated Vault entry for oncall user with a temporary SSH key (expires 48h). Key label: oncall-alex-2026-03-17. Also added read-only IAM role for logs access.

devon: Can you confirm PagerDuty access? Last swap I saw a missing escalation policy error.

pagerduty-bot: alex added to schedule oncall-engineering. Ramp start: 2026-03-17T18:00Z. PagerDuty access: true.

sam: Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/oncall/primary-checks
Also sanity commands to run before you start:
```
# check VPN route to jumpbox subnet
ip route get 10.0.5.1
# ssh via Bastion with temp key
ssh -i ~/.ssh/oncall-alex ubuntu@jumpbox.internal
```

jess: VPN route looks good from my side. Heads-up: corp-kms key-rotation will prompt MFA when a new key is used. Maria — did you add an exception for the 48h key?

maria: Yep — 48h exception applied for oncall users. Audit record: https://vault.redwood/audit/entries/3321. No MFA prompt for this key.

alex: Two quick asks: 1) Someone validate logs access using the new IAM role (read-only) 2) run a low-traffic alert test in staging so we verify paging path.

devon: I'll validate logs access (CloudWatch group /redwood/runtime) now and run the staged alert test in ~10m. @sam can you watch latency on the routing?

sam: Watching. Triggering alert test now: ALERTTEST id=rdw-test-091

sre-bot: ALERT fired rdw-test-091 -> routed to oncall-engineering. No downstream errors detected.

devon: Logs access confirmed — can read /redwood/runtime and tail recent entries (last 6h). No permission errors. :thumbsup: 

alex: Great. Leaving handoff note in the runbook: "handoff verified: vpn, ssh, pager, logs". Escalation order: devon -> jess.

maria: Added a sticky note in the runbook and uploaded the temp key metadata. Good luck! :rocket:

alex: Thanks team — taking the handoff now.
